intent: Practise one-to-one correspondence up to 8 objects by moving items as they are counted to keep track of counted vs uncounted objects.

data.title: Moving Butterflies
data.description: Practise one-to-one correspondence by recounting butterflies as they move to new spots.

challenges.instruction: Count the butterflies. Then watch them move!
challenges.hint: Tap each butterfly one at a time as you count them.
challenges.narration: Let's count these lovely butterflies lined up together.

challenges.instruction: Count the butterflies. Then watch them move!
challenges.hint: Touch each butterfly slowly to keep track of your count.
challenges.narration: Now let's count this line of butterflies.

challenges.instruction: Count the butterflies. Then watch them move!
challenges.hint: Keep counting carefully from the beginning to the end.
challenges.narration: Wonderful! Let's count this new set of butterflies.

challenges.instruction: Count the butterflies. Then watch them move!
challenges.hint: Take your time and touch each butterfly as you count.
challenges.narration: Let's count this larger group of butterflies together.

challenges.instruction: Count the butterflies. Then watch them move!
challenges.hint: Count every single butterfly to make sure you get the right total.
challenges.narration: You are doing amazing. Let's count this final line of butterflies!

judgement.reasoning: The obstacle is losing track (double-counting or skipping objects). The generated task puts objects in a line and activates 'highlightOnTap' and 'showRunningCount', which visually tracks counted vs uncounted items. However, the generator chose 'recount_moved' (a conservation task) rather than moving items to sort counted from uncounted, though the line arrangement with highlight visual feedback effectively addresses the tracking issue.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would use this detour because the linear arrangement and highlight-on-tap feature directly scaffold one-to-one correspondence and prevent double counting.
